chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from one whom he mentioned, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The thief is not subjected to amputation in a year of dearth for anything edible, such as bread, meat, and the like.

key_terms.أَشْبَاهِهِ: things similar to it, comparable edible items
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief, the person accused of theft
key_terms.سَنَةِ الْمَحْقِ: a year of dearth or severe scarcity
key_terms.شَيْءٍ يُؤْكَلُ: something edible, food fit to be eaten

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment for theft applied when someone steals food during a famine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the hadd punishment for theft is not carried out during a time of severe scarcity when the stolen item is food. It indicates consideration of hardship and necessity in applying judicial rulings.
